evidence: DeepSeek uses `if p1_list[i] + p2_list[i] > T` and `sum(p1_list) > T`; GPT uses `p1 + p2 > T`, `sum1`, and `sum2`; Qwen and GLM likewise check each job sum and component totals.
affordance_in_statement: Relaxed Scenario A: "Query i is processed alone under the original rules." Relaxed Scenario B: "The compute node (Component 2) is infinitely fast, requiring 0 minutes for all queries" while Component 1 processes "at most one query at any given moment." Relaxed Scenario C: "The storage array (Component 1) is infinitely fast, requiring 0 minutes for all queries" while Component 2 processes "at most one query at any given moment."
secondary_shortcut_name: guaranteed unique certificate and first-match priority
removal_suggestion: A wording-only change cannot remove this affordance without changing the core task: the stated relaxations intrinsically reduce to checking p1+p2 for one job or summing one component over all jobs. To make the task nontrivial, replace the zero-time/alone relaxations with relaxations that still leave a coupled scheduling or ordering problem, while retaining the same output labels and formats.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Directly applies the additive completion-time test for one job and total-load tests for each isolated component.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The three relaxed scenarios explicitly make either one job independent or one component infinitely fast.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Computes p1+p2 for Scenario A and accumulates sum1 and sum2 for Scenarios B and C.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each relaxed scenario leaves only a single sequential resource or a single query.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same per-job sum and component-total lower bounds without performing scheduling.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement says the relaxed scenarios must fail regardless of schedule and removes one entire phase in Scenarios B and C.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks each isolated job, then sums the processing times on the surviving component.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The relaxed systems are explicitly reducible to one job or one single-capacity component.

common_affordance: The relaxed scenarios completely decouple the problem into additive necessary conditions: p1+p2 for an isolated query, sum(p1) for Scenario B, and sum(p2) for Scenario C.
recommended_edit: Replace the explicit "processed alone" and "infinitely fast, requiring 0 minutes" scenarios with relaxations that preserve interaction between both components—for example, relax a scheduling constraint but retain positive processing on both components—so deciding whether the relaxed scenario misses T requires an actual scheduling analysis rather than three additive comparisons.
